metadata.title: It Doesn't Design the App. It Follows the File.
metadata.subtitle: The Build-Zoom-Meeting-SDK-App Skill (Zoom Meeting SDK)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude builds a Zoom meeting into an app, does it design that integration on its own, or is it following a file that already has the platform's rules written down? Lands the carry-out that build-zoom-meeting-sdk-app never decides to build a Zoom integration -- it hands Claude the platform's exact join rules once that decision's already made.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed Claude would design a whole Zoom meeting app from scratch. It doesn't — it follows steps written in a reference file. So: does Claude follow steps for a whole Zoom meeting app?

props.text:

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is called build-zoom-meeting-sdk-app. Inside: a RUNBOOK.md and a SKILL.md, then one folder per platform — android, electron, iOS, Linux, macOS, react-native. Six platforms, one shared reference. The file is the program.

The instructions are steps, and Claude runs them in order. Read the SKILL.md. Execute each step — join the meeting, handle the waiting room, apply the platform's rules. Return the result. No branching, unless a step itself tells it to branch.

This particular skill is a reference, not a decision-maker. It's read only after a build has already been routed to a meeting-embed workflow — that routing happened somewhere else, before this file ever opens. Once it's open, it supplies the platform's exact rules: real meeting joins, auth and join flows, waiting-room handling, meeting-bot patterns, one platform folder at a time. It doesn't choose the platform or decide to embed a meeting at all. It supplies the rules for the one already chosen.

production_viz.label: REFERENCE, NOT DECISION
production_viz.caption: the decision to embed happens elsewhere

beats.narration_text: Build-zoom-meeting-sdk-app never decides to build a Zoom integration — it hands Claude the platform's exact join rules once that decision's already made.

props.quote: Build-zoom-meeting-sdk-app never decides to build a Zoom integration — it hands Claude the platform's exact join rules once that decision's already made.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I've already decided to add a video call to my app, and I've picked the platform. Before you write any integration code, walk me through the platform's exact rules for joining a call, handling a waiting room, and any bot behavior I need to account for. That's the same order build-zoom-meeting-sdk-app follows — the decision to embed comes first, the platform's rules come after.
